answer: Make the registration fee rise in steps for identities from the same source cluster. The first 100 pay 1 unit each, the next 100 pay 2 each, and the fee doubles every 100 after that, so identities 901 to 1,000 pay 512 each. A farm registering 1,000 fake identities from one cluster therefore spends 102,300 units instead of 1,000, and its last identities cost far more than they can earn. The dune of cheap accounts never forms because the river of registrations from one cluster gets steeper as it grows, and a cipher bound to each cluster keeps the count honest when the same hardware returns.
